evidence.text: Describes Shang oracle forms as variable, with detailed and abbreviated depictions of vehicle features including wheels, body/frame, crossbar, and yoke; says later writing selected some features to form regular 車. Its page displays oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and seal-script categories. This supports pictographic formation and graphic reduction, without implying every version includes every named part.
evidence.title: 漢字「車」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: Reports variable oracle-bone and bronze forms depicting vehicle features, and that bronze forms are often written vertically. It identifies oracle-bone examples for vehicle use in Heji 11452 (“six vehicles”), vehicle-and-horse use in Heji 11450, and a place-name use in Heji 584. It reports bronze vehicle and war-chariot uses, and later Warring States bamboo-slip vehicle and chariot-punishment uses. These are inscription identifiers and source interpretations; the inspected page does not supply calendar dates for each.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 車

evidence.field: graphic variants and dated bronze exemplars
evidence.text: Lists oracle-bone examples by corpus references and bronze examples with period labels, including late Shang and Western Zhou. The page’s interpretation describes oracle forms with differing combinations of canopy, axle, wheels and vehicle body, and later verticalized forms. It classifies the graph as pictographic. This is a secondary reference and its detailed part-by-part interpretation is not independently demonstrated by the page.
evidence.title: 車字形演变字源_汉字「車」_車的甲骨文_車的金文_金文编_甲骨文编

evidence.field: Shang oracle glyph candidate and provenance
evidence.text: The file page identifies the image as a modern SVG representation of 車 in Shang oracle script style. It names source databases and points to a specific Hanziyuan oracle image and Academia Sinica database image as references. The Commons page states CC0/public-domain dedication for the file; this is a redraw, not an artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:車-oracle.svg

evidence.field: Western Zhou bronze glyph candidate and provenance
evidence.text: The file page identifies the image as a modern SVG representation in Western Zhou bronze script style, citing the Hanziyuan image B19579 and Academia Sinica image 34.E39B (noted as 同卣, mid-Western Zhou). The Commons page states CC0/public-domain dedication for the redraw; it is not a photograph or direct scan of the bronze artifact.
evidence.title: File:車-bronze-5.svg

evidence.field: Shuowen seal glyph candidate and provenance
evidence.text: The page identifies a modern SVG redraw of 車 in Shuowen seal-script style and cites Hanziyuan image s10685. It states the representation is public domain. This candidate can illustrate the later standardized seal-script shape, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:車-seal.svg

evidence.text: The Commons glyph pages identify CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication. The license deed permits copying, modification, distribution, and commercial use without requesting permission, to the extent allowed by law.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org 車 oracle bone script file; 車 甲骨文 字形 图片 金文 字形 evolution; site:chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw 車 字形演變
search_audit.outcome: Search returned paleographic descriptions and image leads. Opened Academia Sinica, CUHK, and Guoxuedashi pages; SFTJ page open returned an internal error.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File: 車 oracle bone character; Wikimedia Commons 車 seal script character glyph; Wikimedia Commons 車 bronze inscription character
search_audit.outcome: Opened all three Commons file description pages and inspected image identity, cited sources, and reuse statements. Direct Special:FilePath opens returned internal errors; the file pages nevertheless provide original-file links and rights descriptions.

gaps: No calendar date for the individual oracle-bone examples Heji 11452, 11450, or 584 was given on the inspected CUHK page.
The page supports vehicle and war-chariot senses in early inscriptions, but it does not establish a dated sequence or semantic links for later machine, transport, or measure senses.
The inspected external sources support 車 as pictographic. No semantic/phonetic component pair applies, and no component pronunciation comparison is relevant.

Whole-word loan proposals in the dossier were not reverified in this pass. The original depicted vehicle’s spoken name is not established from its pictograph; reconstructed Chinese pronunciation alone would not prove borrowing from a proposed external vehicle term.

Commons image candidates are modern vector redrawings based on cited paleographic databases. Their identity and rights provenance were checked from descriptions; their pixels were not visually inspected in this research stage.
The Commons Special:FilePath attempts failed to open directly, though original SVG links are provided on the opened file-description pages.

items.tradition: Oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw based on cited paleographic database exemplars
items.caption: An oracle-script form of 車. Early versions vary in how they depict the vehicle’s wheels, frame, and other features.
items.alt: Modern black-line vector redraw of an oracle-bone script form of 車.
items.selection_reason: Shows the graph’s early pictographic character and reported variation.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on Commons file page.

items.period: Western Zhou; cited exemplar identified as mid-Western Zhou
items.tradition: Bronze inscription script; modern vector redraw based on cited 同卣 inscription exemplar
items.caption: A Western Zhou bronze-script form of 車. The more vertical arrangement shows a later graphic presentation of the vehicle pictograph.
items.alt: Modern vector redraw of 車 in Western Zhou bronze script style.
items.selection_reason: Pairs with the oracle form to show graphic change across early writing traditions; source page ties it to an identified bronze inscription exemplar.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, as stated on Commons file page.

items.period: Qin/Han seal-script tradition as represented in the Shuowen seal form
items.tradition: Shuowen seal script; modern vector redraw from a cited database glyph
items.caption: The seal-script form transmitted in the Shuowen tradition, showing a more regularized shape of 車.
items.alt: Modern vector redraw of 車 in Shuowen seal-script style.
items.selection_reason: Offers a later, more regularized point of comparison after the early oracle and bronze forms.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the modern SVG representation, as stated on Commons file page.

limitations.text: These are digital redrawing candidates rather than photographs of original artifacts. Their proposed captions rely on Commons file descriptions and paleographic source pages; no visual inspection of image pixels was performed.
